structured_output.world_model:
W5 (contrarian), after E039. The tip is E036: 5.314 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. On fresh seeds 13–22 it scored 0.7525, so the population mean is about 0.7525–0.753. That is about 0.25 pp above the official bar of 0.75 but below the 3-seed gate of 0.753. Every further time cut has to be paid for with accuracy, and the boosters have not supplied any.

1. Stem truncation saves time because the stem is memory-bandwidth-bound.
- E028 removed group-1 backward and saved about 27% of a 32 px step, for about 20% of conv MACs.
- E036's whitening detach saved 2.4%.
- E037 moved the freeze to 60%. It saved 0.245 s (about 7 ms per truncated step) but cost about 0.4 pp.
- E039 folded group-1 BN. It saved only 0.03 s and lost about 0.2 pp, which looks like noise plus a real cost from eval-mode BN. The cheap part of the stem is now used up.
- Mechanism nobody has stated: group-1 BN in train mode during the frozen phase keeps adapting its batch statistics to the 32 px input distribution. That free adaptation is probably what made E028/E036 accuracy-neutral and what E039 destroyed. The freeze cliff (E037) may come less from the frozen conv weights and more from too few train-mode BN steps after the 28→32 switch. I062 freezes only conv1 and leaves BN1 adaptive, so it is the cleanest test of this.

2. Resolution:
- Early low resolution is cheap but not free. E033 moved 10% of steps from 24 to 20 px, saved 0.19 s and cost about −0.1 pp.
- The 28/32 px tail carries the accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
- The 20 px steps are now the cheapest remaining time, at roughly 8 ms per step removed. Removing them still costs about 0.05–0.1 pp per 10 steps. That rate is similar to the epoch dial, so non-uniform trims are only slightly better than uniform ones.

3. Noise:
- A 3-seed mean has an SD of about 0.15 pp. A math-identical change re-rolls the seeds because of cudnn and atomics nondeterminism (E035).
- A 10-seed held-out mean has an SD of about 0.08 pp.
- Each held-out-gated keep carries about 0.07–0.1 pp of winner's curse (E038).

4. End-of-training boosters keep failing: averaging strength (E025), reset interval (E030), label-smoothing drop (E032), warm-up (E029). The airbench dynamics are locally optimal on this recipe. I expect BN recalibration (I064) to give at most about +0.1 pp: the final Lookahead copy already averages BN buffers over about 20 steps, near-final, with very similar fast weights.

5. Muon has no wd, renormalizes the filters every step, and already uses 3 Newton-Schulz steps. So filter wd is inert and H1.2.3's 'reduce to 3 NS steps' lever is already spent.

6. Fixed costs are tiny. E035 saved 0.035 s, and the rest of trial 0's overhead is worth at most about 0.02 s on the mean.

7. Submission arithmetic: the 3-seed gate needs about 0.753. From 0.7525 that needs about +0.15–0.2 epoch (+0.1 s). Any cut has to be paired with a top-up, so the net Pareto gain per lever is about 0.05–0.1 s.

Unsure:
- The compute vs bandwidth split (I058). I expect non-GEMM ≥30% and stem ≥35% of a 32 px step.
- How much the PCIe judge discounts the bandwidth-bound levers.
- Whether the BN-adaptation mechanism or the conv-weight mechanism explains the freeze cliff.

forecasts.reason: E028's 27% step saving from group-1 backward implies stem plus whitening is about 40% of a 32 px step, and BN/GELU in fp16 at batch 2000 should be ≥30% non-GEMM; the recipe is unchanged, so the metrics repeat the tip.
E033's analogue saved about 0.19 s and cost about 0.1 pp; the time cut is ≥2.5%, but a 0.1–0.15 pp loss sits right at the threshold, and the keep gate (held-out ≥0.7545) is very unlikely to pass.
12 cheap 20 px steps save about 0.1 s; the LR/Lookahead stretch and the RNG re-roll make a ≤0.1 pp loss unresolvable with 10 seeds.
Only conv1 wgrad plus pool/BN1 backward for about 35 steps (about 0.07 s); BN1 stays adaptive in train mode, so the loss should be smaller than E037's, but it is not separable from noise.

About 12 extra truncated steps at about 7 ms each is about 0.08 s; freezing right at the 32 px switch removes BN/conv adaptation to the new resolution, so I expect about −0.1 to −0.2 pp, failing the gate.
The Lookahead-averaged BN buffers near the end already match the near-converged averaged weights; recalibration gains ≤0.1 pp, short of the 0.15–0.2 pp claim, and costs about 0.04 s.
At 16 px, group 3 runs on 1×1 maps where 3×3 filters train only the centre tap; tiny maps also under-use the tensor cores, so the time saving is under 2% and the loss is about 0.15–0.2 pp.
At most about 0.07 s on trial 0 is about 0.02 s on the mean, below H3.2's 0.05 s threshold; nondeterminism may re-roll accuracy slightly.

cruxes: Is the freeze cliff (E037) caused by frozen conv weights or by too few train-mode BN adaptation steps after the 28→32 px switch? I062 (conv1-only freeze, BN1 adaptive) vs I063 separates them, and the answer decides whether earlier freezes can be made nearly free.

What is the accuracy cost per second of removing 20 px steps (I060/I061) compared with the epoch dial? If it is under about 0.5 pp/s, trimming cheap phases and topping up 32 px epochs is a net gain; otherwise the tip is near its Pareto frontier.
Does the PCIe judge keep the bandwidth-bound stem savings (I058 labels)? If its HBM-to-compute ratio differs, the time ranking between the freeze levers and the resolution/epoch levers may flip.
